title: Pixels2Actions
hook: A leading controller failed *all 44 flips*. This one, none. How?
cta: How one GPU beat 128, and the reality check: full episode, link below

segments.label: PAPER
segments.headline: How a humanoid learned flips in its head

beats.narration: On the authors' benchmark, a leading controller, SONIC, fails all forty-four flips. SuperMimic fails none. How?
direct: On the authors' benchmark, a leading controller, SONIC, fails all forty-four flips. SuperMimic fails none. How?

beats.narration: It's SuperMimic, one Berkeley controller for over a hundred twenty-nine thousand motions.
direct: It's SuperMimic, one Berkeley controller for over a hundred twenty-nine thousand motions.

beats.narration: First, it learns a model of how the robot's body moves, from simulator data.
direct: First, it learns a model of how the robot's body moves, from simulator data.

beats.narration: Then it practices inside that model, like rehearsing in your head, and the model shows exactly which way to adjust.
direct: Then it practices inside that model, like rehearsing in your head, and the model shows exactly which way to adjust.

visual.sub: short imagined runs inside the learned model

beats.narration: The result: after nine point eight hours on two GPUs, zero flips failed.
direct: The result: after nine point eight hours on two GPUs, zero flips failed.

beats.narration: In the authors' words: trained in imagination, zero-shot to reality, on a real Unitree G1.
direct: In the authors' words: trained in imagination, zero-shot to reality, on a real Unitree G1.
